propositions: Commit messages with body lines exceeding 72 characters or subjects exceeding 50 characters must be rejected locally at commit time.
A local commit-msg hook checker (check_commit_message_wrap.py) must enforce the 50/72 rule without mutating the message, naming each offending line by position and length.
Gerrit's own commit-msg hook (which stamps Change-Id) must be preserved and chained as commit-msg.legacy, not clobbered by pre-commit install.

Specific line types must be exempt from the 72-character limit: trailers (pattern ^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9-]*:\s), tags (^[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]*=), fenced code blocks, indented literal blocks (4+ leading spaces or tab), table rows (^\|), and lines where length derives from unsplittable atomic tokens (URLs, paths, dotted identifiers).
The make hooks target must verify both pre-commit and commit-msg hook files are installed, warn if Change-Id stamping is missing, and exit non-zero if either hook file is absent.
Git scaffolding (comment lines and --verbose diff below >8 marker) must produce no false positives when checking wrapping.
